claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. His name is Alex and he's 18 years old. He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18 years old, I need to understand his current situation to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(For example, is he attending college, sixth form, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is in approved education, that's relevant to his eligibility.

**Are you responsible for Alex - meaning, does he live with you and/or are you supporting him financially (for example, paying for food, clothes, pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here at home with me and I support him - I pay for everything he needs like food, clothes, and his other expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Now I need to understand your residency status:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Although Alex is 18 years old (over 16), you can still qualify for Child Benefit because:
- Alex is under 20 years old
- He's in approved education (doing his A-levels at college)
- You're responsible for him - he lives with you at home and you support him financially
- You live in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important note:** Your Child Benefit eligibility will continue as long as Alex remains in approved education or training and is under 20 years old. If his circumstances change (for example, if he finishes his education, starts working 24 hours or more per week, or starts claiming certain benefits in his own right), you should notify HMRC as this could affect your eligibility.

Also, be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

Under the UK Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, but you'll still qualify if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training. Alex meets this criterion as he is 18 and in college. The claimant is responsible for Alex as he lives with them and they support him financially (paying for food, clothes, and other expenses). The claimant lives in the UK, which is a requirement for eligibility. No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, which is necessary as only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. Therefore, the claimant meets all the eligibility requirements for claiming Child Benefit for Alex.
